title: Hearty Creamy Kenyan Dum Skillet
description: A comforting and flavorful Kenyan-inspired dish featuring dum, pineapple juice, and a rich creamy sauce, perfect for a sick day or a cozy evening in. This plant-based friendly recipe is made in a cast-iron skillet for a satisfying and filling meal.

ingredients.name: dum
ingredients.notes: Kenyan dum, also known as mandazi, can be found in African markets or online

ingredients.name: curry powder
ingredients.notes: Kenyan-style curry powder or substitute with a similar blend

instructions: Heat a large cast-iron skillet over medium heat and add the chopped onion, cooking until softened and translucent.
Add the minced garlic and cook for an additional minute, stirring constantly to prevent burning.
Add the dum to the skillet, stirring to coat with the onion and garlic mixture.
Pour in the pineapple juice, coconut milk, tomato paste, curry powder, salt, and black pepper, stirring to combine.
Bring the mixture to a simmer and cook for 20-25 minutes, or until the dum is cooked through and the sauce has thickened.
Stir occasionally to prevent scorching and add more pineapple juice or coconut milk if the sauce becomes too thick.
Taste and adjust the seasoning as needed.
Garnish with chopped fresh cilantro and serve hot over rice or with naan bread.
Leftovers can be refrigerated for up to 3 days and reheated as needed.
